items.claim: The row's central philological claim -- that the B-colon noun carries a rarer negative sense rather than its usual positive one -- is never anchored to a verse-specific citation.
items.evidence: boundary_evidence_refs cites only the parent-collection identity span (web:Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16); no ref to web:Prov.14.34 or oshb:Prov.14.34 itself supports the claim that וְחֶ֖סֶד (oshb:Prov.14.34, byte tier) carries the rarer reproach sense rather than covenant-kindness. The collection-span ref establishes C2 membership only, not the lexical crux the rationale is built on; the homograph reading itself is a defensible, well-known crux (cf. the Lev 20:17 negative use), but it ships with zero verse-level evidentiary anchor.

items.claim: The disclosed rival is not the strongest one: 15:7 and 15:14 could never form a valid contiguous cluster span with 15:12, while the true adjacent neighbors go untested in prose.
items.evidence: 15:7 and 15:14 sit non-adjacent to 15:12; any row spanning either into 15:12 would have to absorb unrelated intervening verses (15:8-11, or 15:13), so rejecting them is not a live granularity test. The true adjacent neighbors, 15:11 and 15:13, share no skeleton token with 15:12 on a word-bound check against consonantal_index.json, so single_proverb still holds -- but rejected_alternative never names the verses that actually border the row.

items.claim: observed_substrate_signals overstates לֵ֣ב's grammatical role: it is not the subject of both cola.
items.evidence: In the A-colon לֵ֣ב שָׂ֭מֵחַ is the subject phrase (a glad heart); in the B-colon לֵ֣ב sits inside the construct/adverbial phrase וּבְעַצְּבַת לֵ֝ב ('by grief of heart', oshb:Prov.15.13, byte tier), while the clause subject is ר֣וּחַ נְכֵאָֽה ('spirit crushed'). So 'lev' recurs as a lexeme across the verse but is not 'the constant subject of two different fates' in both halves. The antithetic verdict itself is unaffected by this correction.

items.claim: The ketiv/qere identification is inverted, and the row discloses the cross-seam 'lev' catchword with neither neighbor.
items.evidence: The rationale calls דָּ֑עַת 'the inline ketiv token' and calls ופני 'the qere'; the bytes show the opposite. דָּ֑עַת carries full niqqud and cantillation -- an ordinary pointed word, no part of the K/Q pair at all. ופני is wholly unpointed (zero codepoints in the niqqud/accent range) -- that is the actual ketiv -- and the pointed וּפִ֥י immediately following it is the actual qere (kq inventory: one note at Prov.15.14, pmarks_Prov.json) -- an inline unpointed ketiv immediately preceding its pointed qere, mislabeled in both directions here. Separately, לֵ֣ב recurs verse-initial in both neighbors -- לֵ֣ב שָׂ֭מֵחַ opens 15:13 and וְטֽוֹב לֵ֝֗ב closes 15:15 (word-bound skeleton token 'lev', consonantal_index.json) -- a cross-seam tie the sibling row for 15:13 discloses and rejects as too generic to carry a cluster, but this row never mentions in either direction.

items.claim: The forward boundary against 15:16-17 is tested and correctly disclosed, but the backward cross-seam catchword with 15:14 is never mentioned.
items.evidence: וְטֽוֹב לֵ֝֗ב ('cheerful of heart') at 15:15 shares the exact skeleton token 'lev' with לֵ֣ב at the head of 15:14 (word-bound check, consonantal_index.json) -- a live cross-seam catchword tie -- yet neither the rationale nor rejected_alternative addresses the 15:14 boundary at all, even though the forward test against the tov-min comparative construction of 15:16-17 is handled correctly and explicitly.

items.claim: The proverb_cluster call is well-grounded: a genuine construction run, not a topical resemblance.
items.evidence: Both verses open with the exact skeleton token tov as a comparative predicate and close with a matching two-word tag: 15:16 ends וּמְה֥וּמָה בֽוֹ and 15:17 ends וְשִׂנְאָה בֽוֹ (oshb bytes, re-collated against verse_map_oshb.json) -- the same head noun ('in it') with a different abstract noun (trouble / hatred). The backward boundary against 15:15 (whose tov is a bare adjective, not the tov-min comparative) and the forward boundary against 15:18 (no shared token) both hold on independent re-derivation, and a consecutive tov-min construction run of exactly this shape is one of the recognized classes of byte-grounded cohesion evidence for this collection.

items.claim: single_proverb is correctly argued: the true adjacent rival (15:22) is tested and accurately shown to share no token, and the non-adjacent ma'aneh thread is properly relegated to texture.
items.evidence: 15:22 and 15:23 share no skeleton token on word-bound check; the ma'aneh link to 15:1 and 16:1 is real at the skeleton tier but correctly never argued as a boundary driver since neither verse is adjacent to 15:23, and 16:1 is properly present in boundary_evidence_refs because it is named in device_notes.

items.claim: single_proverb holds on both boundaries, and the paseq disclosure is accurate and correctly tiered as corroboration only.
items.evidence: 15:24 shares no token with 15:25 (correctly untested in prose since there is nothing to disclose); the forward rival 15:26 is tested and correctly shown to share only the generic YHWH token; the paseq claim matches pmarks_Prov.json exactly (Prov.15.25: 1 seg) and is properly disclosed as single-witness corroboration, never a boundary driver.
